SUMMARY
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 5, is issuing this Sources Sought Notice to identify vendors that are interested in and capable of providing the required services.
The Washington DC VA Medical Center requires a contractor to provide a Parking Gate System Replacement, Remote Monitoring, PIV Badge Reader Integration and 5 year Service Agreement for the facility. Interested vendors should review the Statement of Work (SOW) to determine the specific services required.
NCO 5 is seeking responses from firms that are interested in this procurement and possess the resources, capabilities, and qualifications necessary to perform these services.

STATEMENT OF WORK
Parking Gate System Replacement, Remote Monitoring, PIV Badge Reader Integration and Service Agreement 
Department of Veterans Affairs  |  Washington DC VA Medical Center
50 Irving Street NW, Washington, DC 20422
Draft dated October 27, 2026
1. BACKGROUND
The Washington DC VA Medical Center (VAMC) controls vehicle access to its parking areas, service drives and the separated Fisher House locations through nineteen (19) automated gates: eighteen (18) barrier-arm gates and one (1) slide gate at Utility Building 8. The existing gate operators are at end of service life, depend on in-ground loop detectors in deteriorated asphalt, and experience frequent vehicle strikes and extended downtime. The existing card readers at the gates are not uniformly capable of reading Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials, and VA Police Service cannot centrally manage parking-area access.
VA requires (a) replacement of the gate operating equipment with commercial, high-duty equipment and above-ground vehicle detection, (b) remote status monitoring, event cameras and remote gate control for authorized VA personnel, (c) all-new PIV badge readers at each gate, furnished and installed by Johnson Controls, Inc. (JCI) as a subcontractor to the prime, and integrated into the VA Police Service physical access control system (PACS) so VA Police can control access to the facility parking areas, and (d) a firm-fixed-price service agreement covering a base year plus four (4) one-year option periods.
2. SCOPE OF WORK
The Contractor shall furnish all management, supervision, labor, equipment, materials, tools, transportation, subscriptions, and subcontracted services (including the mandatory JCI subcontract in Section 5) necessary to remove the existing gate equipment and furnish, install, test, commission, warrant, monitor, and maintain a complete and operational parking gate and access control system at the 19 gate locations, in accordance with this SOW, manufacturer requirements, and the referenced codes and standards. Equipment brand names in this SOW, other than the JCI/PACS requirement in Section 5, are "or equal."

4. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS   GATE SYSTEM
4.1 Removal and Disposal
Remove existing operators, arms, controls, and abandoned detectors at all 19 locations; legally dispose of all removed material off VA property (batteries recycled per EPA/DC regulations). Clean and prepare concrete pads.
Removal and replacement shall be sequenced so that no parking area loses all vehicle access at once without a VA Police-approved traffic plan.
